title: Interpretation ledger
description: state/interpretation_ledger.json — owned by prompts/33_thesis_synthesis.md, audited by prompts/34_thesis_redteam.md (checks 16-18). docs/OPINION_VS_ANALYSIS.md sections 1-6 separate analysis from opinion; this file handles the case they do not cover, where two competent readers agree on a verified fact and disagree about what it means. A P/E of 30 is expensive against a 10-year median of 18 and cheap at a PEG of 1.0; both are arithmetic on the same disclosed numbers. What settles it is a named conditioning variable and a named discriminator, and this is where both are recorded. An entry that cannot be discriminated is not deleted — it becomes a disclosed load-bearing assumption, which under config.report.stance evidence_first is worth more to a reader than a verdict with nothing behind it.

as_of.description: ISO date of the synthesis pass that wrote this ledger

sector_playbook.description: Playbook slug from config/sector_registry.yaml. Determines which valuation convention the readings are judged against.

entries.description: One entry per valuation-relevant fact whose reading is load-bearing. An empty array fails check 16 — a thesis with no contested facts has not been tested.

conditioning_variable.description: Closed vocabulary, docs/OPINION_VS_ANALYSIS.md section 7.4. Kept in machine form under interpretation_vocabulary.conditioning_variables in config/sector_registry.yaml; E13 in tools/validate_sector_registry.py rejects anything outside it.

verdict.description: What this reading concludes from the fact, in one line. 'Expensive: 67% premium to its own 10-year median of 18x.'

reasoning.description: The arithmetic or mechanism that gets from the fact to the verdict via the conditioner. Not rhetoric — a reader must be able to reproduce it.

who_holds_it.description: Optional attribution: 'consensus', 'management guidance', a named broker, or 'ours'. Attribution is not evidence; it only tells the reader whose view is being represented.

is_ours.description: True for the reading the note adopts. Exactly one reading per entry should carry this.

discriminator.description: The evidence that settles between the readings. Section 7.2 admits exactly four types; tone, consensus, 'the market is wrong' and analyst conviction are not among them.

evidence.description: The actual base rate, distribution, mechanism or dated observable. With type none_available, state what evidence WOULD settle it and why it could not be obtained.

fact_ids.description: Fact IDs backing the discriminator. Module 33 introduces no new facts.

review_date.description: Required in spirit for type forward_observable — the date by which the observation resolves the divergence.

resolved.description: True only when the discriminator actually settles it. Check 18 downgrades a true here with type none_available, or with empty evidence, to false.

fact.description: The verified quantity or disclosed mechanism, stated so that nobody disputes it. 'Trailing P/E is 30.2x on FY26 reported EPS of 41.3.'

fact_source.description: Where the fact came from — a fact ID, a filing reference, or facts/market_data.json. Analysis layer, per section 1: this must be checkable and binary.

readings.description: At least two. One reading is not a divergence — check 17 fails an entry where our reading is the only reading on record, which is failure mode F3 in a new costume.

our_reading.description: Which reading the note adopts and why the discriminator supports it. Where resolved is false, say that plainly and point at the load-bearing assumption it becomes.

sector_convention_applied.description: The convention from prompts/sector_playbooks/<slug>.md that conditions this reading. Section 7.3: the same multiple carries different default verdicts in different sub-sectors, and the playbook is where that default lives.

materiality.description: How much of the thesis turns on this entry. A high-materiality entry with resolved false must appear in the note's load-bearing assumptions and in the rating's capped_by.

becomes_load_bearing_assumption.description: Set true when the divergence is unresolved and the thesis proceeds anyway. Section 7.5: this is a legitimate outcome, but only when disclosed.

pillar_ref.description: Which thesis pillar in state/thesis.json this entry conditions, if any.
